### B.3 What each system leaves open

| System | What it provides | What it leaves open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Google Maps Platform Air Quality API** | Not disclosed. Recommendations for the general public and for children, elderly, pregnant women, athletes, and people with asthma or heart conditions | No uncertainty or confidence documented for forecasts; data sources and method undisclosed; recommendations are text keyed to index level; no stated guarantee on advisory error; closed. |
| **Google Air View+ (India)** | Multi-layer AI fusion. Follows National AQI categorisation and guidance | Nowcast rather than next-day forecast in the sources reviewed; no cohort-specific guidance, uncertainty or explanation documented; closed. |
| **SAFAR-India (IITM / IMD)** | Chemistry-transport modelling. Health advisory and precautions keyed to AQI | Four cities; advisory is generic by AQI level rather than by cohort; no uncertainty communicated. |
| **Air Quality Early Warning System, Delhi (Jena et al.)** | WRF-Chem with chemical data assimilation | Delhi only; computationally heavy physical model; no personalised guidance; no uncertainty band for the public. |
| **Decision Support System v1.0, Delhi (Govardhan et al.)** | WRF-Chem source apportionment | Delhi only; scenarios are sector emission interventions, not translated into who is affected; no cohort or uncertainty layer. |
| **UrbanEmissions.info India air quality forecasts** | WRF + CAMx chemical transport | Physical-model forecast without station-level statistical correction, cohort guidance or uncertainty in the sources reviewed. |
| **CPCB National AQI portal and Sameer app** | Index computed from measurements. Health statements attached to each AQI category | Describes the present, not tomorrow; one message for everyone in a category; the maximum sub-index discards the rest of the mixture. |
| **Graded Response Action Plan (CAQM)** | n/a (decision protocol). Population-wide restrictions by stage | Triggers on a single regional AQI threshold; no differentiation by vulnerable group; forecast uncertainty is not part of the stated trigger. |
| **US EPA AirNow and the Air Quality Flag Program** | Agency forecasts. Guidance for sensitive groups (lung disease, older adults, children, people active outdoors); school flag colours drive activity changes | Two tiers only (everyone / sensitive groups); timing guidance is generic; no uncertainty shown. |
| **UK Daily Air Quality Index** | Operational forecast. Separate advice for the general population and for at-risk individuals (lung problems, heart problems, older people) | Two tiers; advice keyed to band rather than to the pollutant mixture; no uncertainty shown. |
| **Air Quality Health Index, Canada (Stieb et al.)** | Sum of excess mortality risk across pollutants, scaled 0-10. Index is itself health-derived | Coefficients are Canadian; no cohort-specific weights; a framework to follow rather than a competitor. |
| **Hong Kong Air Quality Health Index** | Health-risk based index. Precautionary advice for children, the elderly and people with heart or respiratory illness, separately from the general public | Two tiers; no uncertainty; no scenario analysis. |
| **European Air Quality Index (EEA)** | Index. Health messages for the general population and for sensitive groups | Two tiers; not forecast-driven in the source reviewed. |
| **City-specific AQHI for Delhi and Varanasi (George et al.)** | Generalised additive model, quasi-Poisson. Excess mortality risk per AQI category (2% moderate to 16% severe) | Two cities; retrospective; no forecast, no cohort weights, no application. Shows a pooled index can misrepresent local risk. |
| **Forecaster.health (ISGlobal)** | Epidemiological exposure-response models applied to forecasts. Mortality-risk alerts by sex and age group for PM2.5, PM10, NO2 and O3 | Europe only; groups are sex and age, not condition or occupation; no decision guarantee on warnings or scenario analysis documented. The closest conceptual prior art, and epidemiologically stronger than a hand-weighted index. |
| **IQAir AirVisual** | Described only as machine learning and AI. Health recommendations | Method and accuracy undisclosed; no uncertainty; generic recommendations. |
| **Plume Labs Air Report** | Described as environmental AI. Advice tailored to runners, cyclists, parents and outdoor dining | Activity profiles rather than health-vulnerability cohorts; 24-h horizon; no uncertainty; method undisclosed. |
| **AQI.in** | n/a. Personalised health recommendations by location | No next-day forecast documented in the listing reviewed; no uncertainty or explanation. |
| **Ambee Air Quality API** | Not disclosed | Vendor-reported accuracy; no uncertainty, cohort guidance or explanation documented; closed. |
| **AirRater (Workman et al. evaluation)** | n/a. Personal symptom tracking and alerts | No forecast; evidence is qualitative. Useful as evidence that people with existing conditions act on such information. |
| **ECMWF CAMS global atmospheric composition (via Open-Meteo)** | Physical model | About 45 km grid cannot resolve a city's hotspots; modelled, not measured. The benchmark any Indian statistical forecast must beat. |
| **Aurora foundation model (Bodnar et al.)** | Foundation model, fine-tuned per task | Grid-scale concentrations; no health layer, no decision layer; heavy to run. |
| **AirFormer (Liang et al.)** | Transformer with a stochastic latent stage | Needs a dense station graph; no health layer; uncertainty is modelled internally rather than calibrated for users. |
| **PM2.5-GNN (Wang et al.)** | Knowledge-enhanced graph neural network | Requires a multi-city graph and meteorology; no uncertainty or health layer. |
| **E-STGCN (Panja et al.)** | Graph convolution with extreme-value-guided LSTM; conformal prediction intervals | One city; no health or decision layer; no unseen-city test. The closest Indian work on extremes with conformal intervals. |
| **Probabilistic deep learning to quantify uncertainty in air quality forecasting** | Probabilistic deep learning | Uncertainty reported as a modelling result, not carried into a public advisory. |
| **Conformal prediction of air pollution concentrations, Barcelona Metropolitan Region** | Conformal prediction | Intervals without a decision or advisory layer. |
| **Cross-city transfer learning for Sentinel-5P NO2 (Janku et al.)** | CatBoost, leave-one-city-out | Estimates concentrations rather than forecasting; five wealthy cities; shows leave-one-city-out is already an established protocol. |
| **Spatial transfer learning for estimating PM2.5 in data-poor regions** | Transfer learning | Estimation at unseen locations rather than next-day advisory. |
| **Ambiguity and novelty rejection for time-series forecasting (Feng et al.)** | Error-variance ambiguity rejection plus VAE / Mahalanobis novelty rejection | General method; does not examine which cases are rejected in a safety-critical advisory setting. |
| **Model-agnostic explainable selective regression via uncertainty estimation** | Selective regression | General method, not air quality. |
| **Conformal risk control (Angelopoulos et al.)** | Distribution-free control of an expected loss | Guarantee assumes exchangeability, which a drifting pollution series violates; needs adaptation for time series. |
| **WHO AirQ+** | Epidemiological exposure-response functions. Attributable cases, years of life lost | Desktop assessment tool, not a forecast or advisory system. |
| **US EPA BenMAP-CE** | Exposure-response functions with built-in percentage roll-back of concentrations. Mortality and morbidity avoided, with valuation | Assessment tool; annual-scale outcomes; not connected to a daily forecast or advisory. Direct prior art for percentage-reduction scenarios. |
| **The value of air quality forecasting in the Mid-Atlantic region** | Cost-loss decision model. Protective-action framing | One cost-loss ratio for all users; not cohort-specific; no distribution-free guarantee. |
| **The boy who cried wolf revisited (Roulston and Smith)** | Cost-loss with false-alarm intolerance | Theory; motivates measuring over-warning alongside under-warning. |
| **Random-forest meteorological normalisation (Grange et al.)** | Random forest | Explains why an uncorrected before/after comparison cannot be read causally. |
| **COVID-19 lockdowns cause global air pollution declines (Venter et al.)** | Weather-adjusted comparison. Health-burden implications | The reference method for a lockdown effect; the present project's -34% is not weather-adjusted. |
| **Ambient air pollution and daily mortality in ten cities of India (de Bont et al.)** | Poisson time series with instrumental-variable causal analysis. 1.4% higher daily mortality per 10 ug/m3 (2-day mean); 3.6% in the causal analysis | All-age mortality only; the Indian evidence base an advisory index should be anchored to. |
| **AirSense-X: physics-informed neural and explainable AQI prediction** | Physics-informed neural network with XAI | Headline accuracy near the level a same-day formulation produces by construction; no persistence baseline, uncertainty or unseen-city test in the summary reviewed. |
| **Forecasting and validating Delhi's AQI: a multi-model approach** | Linear, random forest, XGBoost with SHAP | Single station; no weather; no uncertainty. An honest next-day result that shows how hard the task is without lag-rich features. |
| **Dual-branch explainable AI framework for AQI across Indian cities** | XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, linear; LSTM, GRU, TCN, Transformer; multi-level XAI | Model comparison with explanation; no health, uncertainty or decision layer in the summary reviewed. |
| **Student and open projects on the same Kaggle dataset** | Random forest, KNN, gradient boosting, LSTM. None or generic | Commonly predict the same day's AQI from the pollutants that define it, with random splits and no persistence baseline. |
| **Instructor-worker LLM system for air-quality policy recommendation** | Multi-agent large language model. LLM-generated daily health advisories compared against issued ones | Generative advice without a calibrated forecast or an error guarantee. |
| **ESoWC air-quality bias correction of CAMS** | Machine- and deep-learning bias correction | Establishes statistical post-processing of CAMS as a known technique; not India-specific. |
| **Machine learning for urban air quality analytics: a survey** | Review of temporal, spatiotemporal and attention models | Confirms that forecasting architecture alone is a crowded field. |
| **CPCB continuous monitoring data for India, 2015-2019 (Princeton Data Commons)** | n/a | Ends 2019; a station-level complement to the city-level file used today. |
| **AirGuard India 1.0 (this project, as deployed)** | LightGBM regression; LightGBM + SMOTE classification as deployed. Seven-cohort Health Advisory Index with hand-set weights | Not live; no weather; no interval; deployed confidence is miscalibrated; index saturates on bad days; advisory weights unvalidated. |
